claims.text: For shared-model/data/budget optimizer comparisons BELOW task-specific saturation, use cumulative displacement Δ as a progress proxy, not a universal test-loss ranking. Check K1004/K1071-K1073 before choosing maximum Δ. Adam/AdamW/RMSprop: Δ≈lr·T; Adagrad: 2·lr·√T; SGD: lr·T·|g|/(1-m), |g|≈0.01 (bigram 0.003; momentum MSE 0.03, K1019). Older backtests favored larger Δ in ~85% after ceiling exceptions, but not every 256-2048-step task is under-trained. Across different architectures or optimizers, close Δ estimates are not decisive (K1012); use scoped architecture rules. Long-budget spiral/XOR maxima can lose (q_fb4a7f/q_46d72e); no validated general ceiling yet.
claims.mechanism: Displacement estimates optimization progress before saturation; test loss can instead be limited by stability, fine fitting or generalization after sufficient progress. These phases differ by task/model/budget.
claims.phase: progress-limited training; conditional on not being in an evidenced saturation regime

regime.note: Progress proxy, strongest for shared model/data/budget. Check saturation K1004/K1071/K1072/K1073 first; long-budget q_fb4a7f/q_46d72e remain unvalidated as general ceilings.

claims.text: Adagrad vs Adam/AdamW on the SAME architecture/budget: Adagrad Δ≈2·lr·√T, so comparable progress needs lr≈√T/2 (8-23×) higher. At lr_Adagrad/lr_Adam≤3, Adam-family wins65/70; ratio10 is mixed4/7; ratio≥30 Adagrad wins9/9. For shared-architecture Adagrad rate comparisons, larger lr usually wins (original40/41; broader univariate lab73/78, history13/16), not always; lr3e-3 is not a universal safety guarantee. Do not use this rate preference to settle LN/activation changes (q_cd8a07). At lr≤1e-4, Δ≤0.01 over T≤2048 indicates little progress relative to adaptive rates≥3e-5, but freezing is approximate.

SGD (all families): plain SGD (momentum 0) at lr≤3e-3 is nearly frozen (wins ~8% of its appearances; in LMs embedding rows barely move, CE stays ≈ln V). SGD momentum 0.9 behaves like Adam at ~lr/10: so SGD m=0.9 lr 1e-3-3e-3 ≈ Adam 1e-4-3e-4 and is a real contender — it beats Adagrad ≤1e-3, Adam/RMSprop ≤3e-5-1e-4 and unstable RMSprop 3e-3 (e.g. univariate MSE 6e-5 vs 0.03) — but SGD m=0.9 at lr≤3e-4 loses to Adam/RMSprop at the same lr (10× smaller Δ). Family calibration (SGD calibration rule): bigram LM ≈ Adam at lr/30 (weaker), MSE regression ≈ Adam at lr/3 (stronger). Compute Δ with momentum.

LR/Δ exceptions: do NOT assume maximum Δ or lr3e-3 is always safe. MSE RMSprop lr≥1e-3: versus ≥3× smaller Δ, wins22/36 corpus (better MLP6/6, equal12/22, worse4/8); at equal lr prefer Adam (RMSprop3e-3 loses33/35). Univariate lower-RMSprop-rate preference can occur even below this ceiling (K1063). Bigram optima depend on model width (K1071); wide multilayer univariate high-Δ fitting risk is comparative, not automatic last place (K1072). Tabular optimum changes with epochs/data rule (K1073). Short-budget XOR/spiral often benefit from high rates, but T2048 winners q_46d72e/q_fb4a7f refute blanket long-budget safety; no general replacement ceiling is validated.
claims.mechanism: RMSprop's first steps are lr/sqrt(small square-avg) ≈ up to 10× lr with no momentum smoothing; in unnormalized MLPs these kicks inflate hidden activations and the MSE output, so training oscillates. LayerNorm bounds hidden scale (and residual paths keep the function near-identity), absorbing the kicks — predicts instability only when the RMSprop net lacks LN/residual, as observed (6/6 vs 4/8).

regime.note: (a) corpus regression pairs; (b) bigram post-LN transformer vs GRU

claims.phase: RMSprop≥3e-3 vs ≥3× smaller-Δ choice on MSE: RMSprop net has higher LN+residual score → wins 6/6; equal → 12/22; lower → 4/8. RMSprop 1e-3 univariate 1/4.

claims.text: Second-order optimizer knobs are noise at these budgets: weight decay 0-1e-3 changes loss <1% (same-arch pairs: higher wd 3 wins/10 losses, all within 1%); Adam vs AdamW at equal lr/betas is a coin flip (5-5); beta2 0.95 vs 0.999 is ~even (7-4). Never let these override a lr·T difference; in rankings, order such near-twins by architecture or leave them adjacent. EXCEPTION — tasks whose CE can reach ~1e-4 (two-spiral 1-1.5 turns, Adam-family lr≥1e-3): torch Adam with coupled weight_decay≥1e-3 loses to an AdamW or wd=0 twin by 30-500× (K1040, q_6a81f1); β2 there flips with lr, so do not use β2 to explain it.

MLPs at tied optimizer/lr/T and low Δ: compare LayerNorm count, residual status and task-specific exceptions; do NOT score a residual path as exactly one extra LN. For multivariate MSE with both Δ<0.1, a plain net with one extra LN is favored (K1076: lab 23/31, MSE ratio 0.906). Older more-LN corpus counts: multivariate 61/72, univariate 57/69, tabular Δ<0.1 41/45; these are not factor-isolated effects. At equal LN, regression rectifiers are a preference (K1008), not a full ranking rule. Use K1074 for regression depth, K1039 for shared SGD, K1020/K1077 for spirals, K1061 for deep plain tails, K1018/K1065 for XOR, K1009/K1033 for tabular budget reversals.
claims.mechanism: LayerNorm and skips can improve signal propagation, but observed pairwise rankings do not establish a fixed exchange rate between them. Task, activation, depth, optimizer and normalization placement interact.

regime.note: Tied optimizer/lr/T; low displacement; task-specific rules take precedence. Residual is not a full LN point.

claims.phase: LN-count win rate: multivariate 61-11, univariate 57-12 (lab same-residual more-LN: multivariate at 32768 samples 8/9, ratio 0.38; univariate 37/39), tabular Δ<0.1 41-4 but Δ>=0.1 less-LN 17-6 (K1009); residual at equal LN is the weakest term (lab regression 19/29, ratio ~0.96; q_ca0dea plain beat its residual twin); spiral: K1020; XOR plain+LN vs residual 6/10.

claims.text: MSE REGRESSION activation (uni/multivariate): at EQUAL LayerNorm count prefer ReLU/LeakyReLU over SiLU/GELU, even for smooth cubic/sin/cos targets — do not pick SiLU/GELU for 'smoothness matching'. Lab equal-LN multivariate 37/52 (SGD 13/15, MSE ratio ~2; Adam-family 24/37, ratio ~1.1); activation-only univariate Adam-family with ≥2 LN 9/9 (ratio ~14). SiLU is worst (LeakyReLU beat SiLU 7/7 activation-only). Epoch: SiLU/GELU nets ranked last in q_b61944, q_c9738e, q_f2b7b5, q_6495eb. With FEWER LN the rectifier is a coin flip (17/33) — count LN first (K1006); shared SGD see K1039. Flips: tabular classification Δ≥0.1 (K1056), XOR ≥8 features (K1018).
claims.mechanism: SiLU/GELU have slope ~0.5 near 0 (silu(x)≈x/2), so each un-normalized block halves signal and gradient; stacked smooth blocks attenuate more under small-step optimizers (SGD ratio ~2-5 vs Adam ~1.1, Adam rescales gradients). LN restores scale, which is why an extra LN outweighs the activation (17/33). Predicts the penalty grows with depth and with SGD, and vanishes with per-layer normalisation of every block.

regime.note: equal LN count required

claims.phase: Rect vs smooth (multivariate lab): equal LN SGD 13/15, adaptive 24/37; rect with fewer LN 17/33 (coin flip); rect with more LN 12/13. Univariate activation-only: ≥2 LN adaptive 9/9, SGD 5/6; <2 LN adaptive 3/6.

claims.text: Tabular CE, 1024 rows, 2-16 Gaussian features, SHARED optimizer/lr/T and Δ≥0.1: shallow, smooth and fewer-LN are separate empirical preferences, not an additive architecture score. Older corpus: shallow wins 21/26, fewer-LN 17/23, smooth 16/16; combined rule 26/32 arch-only winners. Do not discard a residual+LN advantage solely for smooth activation or width (q_11a5f0); width was not isolated. At Δ<0.1 older more-LN wins 41/45, deeper 35/52, but 32-epoch depth reversals can start near Δ0.03 (K1033). Epochs/data rule matter: see K1073 for optimizer sweet spots and K1056 for activation. These are conditional ranking observations, not proof that every Δ≥0.1 boundary is learned.
claims.mechanism: Observed architecture preferences change with displacement and examples seen, but these rankings do not independently measure boundary fit or confidence calibration. Overconfidence is a competing explanation, not a condition proven solely by Delta.

regime.note: Shared optimizer/lr/T; no additive architecture score or factor-isolated width effect.

claims.phase: Δ_shared<0.1: more LN 41-4, deeper 35-17; Δ_shared≥0.1: shallower 21-5, less-LN 17-6, smooth act 16/16 (counterexample q_87182b: more early LN in residual LeakyReLU won). Across Δ (mixed questions) prefer Δ≈0.1-0.3 over ≥3× larger (K1021).

claims.text: For mixed choices, close cross-optimizer Δ estimates are uncertain; a 25% edge is not decisive (q_77d140). BELOW task/model saturation, ≥4× Δ favors progress over architecture (higher wins35/40 even against ≥2 extra LN/residual). Within ~3×, better architecture wins11/19: a weak preference, not a deterministic rank. Once both Δ≳0.3 extra Δ wins only≈62%; check K1004/K1063/K1071-K1073 and data/budget before sorting by Δ. Near-chance choices (Δ<~0.005: CE≈ln2/lnV, MSE≈Var(y)) are a tied bottom group; use architecture rather than tiny rate differences. No universal RMSprop-over-Adagrad correction is validated for near-parity LM comparisons.
claims.phase: Saturation (smaller Δ≥0.1, larger ≥3×; lab): larger-Δ wins bigram 4/16, tabular 63/146, spiral 54%, multivar 56%, XOR 58%, univar 60%. SGD vs adaptive (lab, calibrated Δ): SGD 1-3× behind but ≥2 more LN wins 90/130; 3-10× behind 61/181; 10-30× 25/95 (vs 19% / 13% without the LN edge).

claims.text: Residual × depth × task: on regression, depth helps even without residuals (deeper plain beats shallower residual 24-15) because composed nonlinearities are needed for curvature; on classification, depth WITHOUT residual hurts (shallower residual beats deeper plain 19-13) while deeper residual beats shallower plain 33-14. So for CE tasks never pick a deep (≥4) plain stack over a residual one at the same optimizer; for MSE tasks a deep plain stack with ≥2 LN blocks is still competitive. Deep residual MLPs win 53% of their appearances vs 29% for deep plain.

Capacity is not the bottleneck: at these budgets parameter count and width barely predict the winner — do not pick the 'biggest model'. Pairwise larger-params wins only 37/76 on bigram LMs, ~50% on univariate regression; at equal depth wider MLPs are a coin flip on regression (5-5) and only mildly better on classification (7-2). Datasets are tiny but noiseless (256-1024 rows), and every candidate has ample capacity; what differs is how fast the parameters move (Δ) and how well signal propagates (LN, residual, activation). Use width/params only as the last tie-breaker (and prefer wider only in the tabular Δ≥0.1 regime).

Bigram LM transformer SHAPE (transformer vs transformer, same optimizer/lr/T; Δ in core-rule units). EQUAL d_model, layer count: 0.1≤Δ<0.5 FEWER layers wins 23/23 (corpus 6/6, lab 17/17; q_ce881e, q_f2011a); Δ≥0.5 fewer 8/11; 0.02≤Δ<0.1 COIN FLIP (fewer 8/15; q_4f69f2, q_9344eb: 2-layer beat 1-layer) - do not decide by depth there; Δ<0.02 deeper wins 19/28. EQUAL depth: larger d_ff is a tie-break worth ~1-2% CE - wins at Δ≤0.1 (11/12; q_f2011a 256>128>64), not above (3/13). DIFFERENT d_model: 0.02≤Δ<0.1 larger wins 15/15; Δ≥0.5 smaller wins 5/6, order by d_model ascending then layers (q_17f213; K1068). GRU vs transformer: K1075; lr: K1071.

XOR CE, 1024 rows, ≥8 features, shared Adam/AdamW/RMSprop lr/T and Δ≥0.05: favor smooth activations (lab 15/16, CE ratio 0.78; corpus 6/6). Do not apply a universal shallow/fewer-LN score. More-LN wins only 8/32 lab but 5/11 corpus; fewer-LN is a preference. Depth depends on residuals (K1065): only the ≥3-block gap favors a ≤2-block net (lab 5/5, ratio 0.51; corpus 2/3). Below Δ0.05, more LN wins 33/41 (ratio 0.93), activation is mixed (smooth 3/8), and depth is conditional. With <8 features do not apply this reversal (deeper 7/7). Δ0.05 separates sampled bands, not a demonstrated sharp causal threshold; SGD/Adagrad extrapolation is unvalidated.
claims.mechanism: A possible explanation is distractor fitting and confidence growth after partial XOR learning. The sampled displacement bands do not independently measure when the XOR interaction is learned, and do not establish a sharp causal boundary at Delta=.05. Depth effects depend on residual status (K1065); activation/LN evidence remains partly architecture-confounded.

regime.note: Shared optimizer/lr/T; independent LN and residual-dependent depth preferences. No sharp boundary established.

claims.phase: nf≥8: Δ≥0.05 smooth 15/16, more-LN 8/32, shallow vs ≥3 deeper 5/5; Δ<0.05 more-LN 33/41, shallow 4/14, smooth 3/8. nf<8: Δ≥0.05 more-LN 4/8, deeper 7/7 corpus + 2/2 lab; Δ<0.05 more-LN 8/11.

claims.text: SGD gradient-scale calibration for the Δ rule (K1001 assumes raw |g|≈0.01), fit on 368 SGD-vs-adaptive pairs. Bigram LM: use |g|≈0.003 (SGD m=0.9 ≈ Adam at lr/30, plain ≈ lr/300): larger-Δ correct 68/70 vs 63/70 at 0.01; SGD m=0.9 beat Adam/AdamW/RMSprop in only 1/18 LM pairs (1/4 even at nominal Δ parity). MSE regression with momentum 0.9: use |g|≈0.03 (SGD m=0.9 ≈ Adam at lr/3): 59/71 vs 54/71; it wins 11/19 when the adaptive Δ is ≤4× its 0.01-estimate. Classification (131/146) and plain-SGD regression: keep 0.01. Plain SGD wins only 3/141 pairs when the adaptive Δ is >15× larger. These calibrations assume the SGD net has ≥1 LayerNorm; 0-LN SGD nets get far less credit (K1038).

TWO-SPIRAL classification MLPs (same optimizer/lr/T): score LN count FIRST, residual as tie-break - UNLESS the residual net is ≥2 blocks DEEPER. Same residual status: more LN wins (lab 163/206, CE ratio 0.79-0.92). Plain-more-LN vs residual-fewer-LN at 0.03≤Δ<0.5: plain wins when depths are within ±1 (lab 58/66, ratio 0.85; q_31abed), but a residual net ≥2 blocks deeper wins (lab 6/8, ratio 0.71; q_40922b: depth-5 residual, Adagrad 3e-3×1024, beat depth-3 plain nets with more LN; K1066). Δ<0.03: coin flip (residual 14/24). Δ≥0.5: residual 5/6. Residual with ZERO LN loses to plain ≥1-LN nets at Δ<0.5 (lab 8/59), wins at Δ≥0.5 (10/13).
claims.mechanism: Each LN rescales block activations to unit RMS, raising the effective step size of the features that bend the boundary; a skip connection preserves the input path but does not speed feature learning. Predicts LN count dominates whenever learning curved features is the bottleneck (most Δ), and residual matters only when plain deep stacks overshoot (high Δ, harder spirals).

regime.note: Δ = core-rule units; 0.1-0.5 and ≥0.5 bands have only 3-5 lab sets

claims.phase: Plain(more LN) vs res(fewer LN), 0.03≤Δ<0.5: depth gap ≤1 → plain 58/66; res ≥2 deeper → res 6/8 (+q_40922b), corpus 0/1. Δ<0.03 res 14/24; Δ≥0.5 res 5/6. Res(0 LN) vs plain(≥1 LN): Δ<0.5 plain 51/59; ≥0.5 res 10/13.

claims.text: LN PLACEMENT tie-breaker (MLP pre-LN blocks): at equal LN count and equal residual status, prefer the net whose last LayerNorm is closer to the output head (fewer unnormalized blocks after the final LN). Holds on synthetic tabular classification and multivariate regression when Δ<0.1: corpus 11/12 pairs (median loss ratio ~0.80); lab 4/7 (ratio ~0.99); controlled smooth-additive test 2/2 (0.95); q_7ae5d3 (tabular, Adagrad ≤3e-4) agrees. Does NOT hold on univariate regression or XOR (corpus 2/8; controlled univariate 1/4) nor at Δ≥0.1 (3/6). Apply only after LN count + residual tie (K1006); whether late placement beats one extra early LN is untested.
claims.mechanism: A pre-LN right before the last hidden Linear restores unit feature scale feeding the head, so tiny updates (Δ<0.1) move the output more; each unnormalized block after it shrinks hidden RMS (~0.5x for SiLU/GELU). Predicts the advantage fades once Δ≥0.1 (feature scale is learned) - observed 3/6. Why univariate/XOR don't follow is unexplained.

regime.note: equal LN count, equal residual, same optimizer/lr/T; small n, effect ~5-20%

claims.phase: late-LN wins: tabular Δ<0.1 corpus 6/7, lab 3/5; multivariate Δ<0.1 corpus 5/5, lab 1/2; any family Δ>=0.1 3/6; univariate 1/4 corpus + 1/4 controlled; XOR 1/4 corpus, 2/4 lab.

claims.text: Tabular depth reversal starts EARLIER with more epochs (synthetic tabular classification, 1024 rows, 16 features): at total_samples_seen=32768 (32 epochs, T=512 bs64) shallow 2-block wide nets beat 4-block nets already at Δ≈0.03-0.1 (Adagrad 1e-3×512 Δ0.045, Adam 1e-4×512): controlled sparse_interaction + smooth_additive, shallow wins 16/16 pairings (median CE ratio 0.59-0.75); q_eeb76a (two 2-block 2-LN plain nets 1st-2nd, 4-block 4-LN residual last). At 4 epochs (T=256 bs16) same Δ is a coin flip (4/8, ratio 0.99). Among shallow nets more LN wins (2-LN plain > 1-LN residual 6/6); among deep, residual > plain (6/6, ratio 0.80). Below Δ 0.03 depth still OK (corpus ≥16 ep: shallow 6/17).
claims.mechanism: Depth adds composed nonlinear capacity that, with only 1024 rows and 12+ noise coordinates, is spent fitting distractor structure once the data has been revisited many times; the overfit cost scales with epochs, not with Δ alone. So the Δ at which shallow-wide nets overtake deep ones falls as epochs rise (4→32). Predicts: at ≤4 epochs the K1009 Δ≥0.1 threshold holds; at Δ<0.03 nets are still boundary-limited and depth/LN help.

regime.note: one instance per family; depth confounded with width/LN; piecewise untested

claims.phase: shallow(2-block) vs deep(4-block), Δ 0.03-0.1: 32 epochs → shallow 16/16 (ratio .59-.75); 4 epochs → 4/8 (.99). Corpus ≥16 epochs: Δ≥0.1 shallow 12/15 (.65); Δ<0.03 shallow 6/17 (1.04).

claims.text: For depth≥3, ZERO-LN SGD MLPs versus a rival with Δ<0.1 and ≥3× smaller calibrated Δ, discount the nominal progress advantage; do not call them frozen or reject all SGD nets. Original within-set lab: larger-Δ zero-LN deep SGD won 21/60 (18 sets), median loss ratio ≈1.0; shallow zero-LN nets did much better (rectifier 80%, smooth 67%). With ≥1 LN, larger-Δ SGD won 493/563 (88%); do not apply the zero-LN penalty there. MSE zero-LN comparisons were only 37/70, so task-specific evidence matters. These are architecture/optimizer-confounded preferences, not a universal gradient bound. Examples: q_bfe225 and q_1469ce; calibration K1019.
claims.mechanism: Unnormalized deep stacks can attenuate hidden activations and raw SGD gradients under default initialization; LayerNorm or adaptive scaling may reduce this problem. This is a candidate explanation for weak nominal-displacement credit, not a measured universal gradient bound. Pooled pairwise rates do not establish that every zero-LN SGD net is frozen, nor that one LN removes all attenuation.

regime.note: SGD net vs rival with >=3x smaller calibrated Δ, rival Δ<0.1; lab within-set pairs

claims.phase: SGD larger-Δ win rate: ≥1 LN 88% (493/563); 0 LN depth≤2 rect 80% (77/96), smooth 67% (60/90); 0 LN depth≥3 35% (21/60). Regression 0-LN 53% (37/70); classification 0-LN 69%.

claims.text: SGD × activation on MSE regression (uni/multivariate, all choices share one SGD optimizer, plain or m=0.9, 256-2048 steps): smooth activations (SiLU, GELU) are penalised far more than under Adam, so activation outranks a ONE-block LN deficit. ReLU/LeakyReLU vs SiLU/GELU: equal LN corpus 9/10 + controlled 8/8 (MSE ratio 0.04-0.5); rectifier with 1 fewer LN wins 14/17 (controlled 6/6, corpus 5/8, q_47a7c4, q_4a2253 LeakyReLU 3-LN beat SiLU 4-LN residual); with ≥2 fewer LN only 12/25 (corpus 1/6; wins mainly on large-offset targets) — keep LN count first (K1006). Deeper SiLU nets lose more (depth5 12/16, depth4 4/8). Under Adam-family keep K1006 (corpus: SiLU with more LN wins 11/16).
claims.mechanism: SiLU'(0)=0.5, so each block halves small-signal gradients; LN fixes forward scale but not this derivative attenuation. SGD has no per-parameter rescaling, so the attenuation directly shrinks effective step size, compounding with depth; Adam's 1/√v undoes it. Predicts: effect grows with SiLU depth (5>4 blocks), vanishes under Adam-family, and cannot overcome a large normalization deficit where LN itself is needed (≥2 LN gap on oscillatory sums).
claims.phase: Rectifier (fewer LN) vs SiLU/GELU (more LN), shared SGD regression: LN gap 0 → 17/18; gap 1 → 14/17; gap ≥2 → 12/25 (corpus 1/6; controlled offset target 6/6, trig 4/12). Adam-family: SiLU-more-LN wins 11/16 (corpus).

claims.text: Only for matched net/lr/budget twins on easy 1-1.5-turn spirals, Adam wd≥1e-3 loses to AdamW or wd=0; this does NOT show wd=1e-4 is safe or rank different recipes. Controlled plain ReLU depth2 width48, lr3e-3, T≈1024: Adam wd1e-3 CE≈0.003, wd1e-2≈0.044, versus AdamW wd1e-3/1e-2 ≤2e-4 and wd=0 3e-5-1.8e-4. AdamW wins 12/12 cells, CE ratio 0.002-0.03. q_6a81f1 supports AdamW over Adam at wd1e-3 on a shared 1-layer GELU net. No validated decay threshold for q_fb4a7f (T2048, different lr/wd), 2-3-turn spirals, RMSprop, Adagrad or bigram LM. Beta2 is a weak lr-dependent tie-break, not an explanation of decay effects.
claims.mechanism: torch Adam adds wd·w to the gradient before dividing by √v. Once the spiral is fit, data gradients→~0, so the decay term dominates both numerator and v and Adam takes ~lr-sized normalized steps toward zero, capping weight norm and logit margin (CE floor ~1e-3). AdamW shrinks by lr·wd·w (~1e-6/step), negligible. Predicts harm grows with wd, lr and T, and vanishes when data gradients stay large (noisy-label bigram LM, under-trained 3-turn spirals).

regime.note: Only matched net/lr/budget twins; coupled Adam wd>=1e-3. No safety conclusion at1e-4; harder spirals untested.

claims.phase: AdamW(wd) vs Adam(coupled wd), same lr/net, spiral: wd1e-3 ratio ~0.03, wd1e-2 ~0.002 (12/12). β2 .999 vs .95 (same wd): lr 3e-3 ratio 5.8, 1e-3 24 (0.95 wins); lr 3e-4 ratio 0.36 (0.999 wins); with LN signs mixed.

claims.text: TABULAR classification (synthetic, 1024 rows), once trained (shared core-rule Δ≥0.1, same optimizer/lr/T): prefer GELU/SiLU over ReLU/LeakyReLU. Smooth wins 23/25 lab within-set pairs (~11 sets, median test-CE ratio ~0.80; smooth_additive 14/14, sparse_interaction 5/6, piecewise 4/5); corpus 16/16 (K1009). At Δ 0.01-0.1 only a tendency (44/74, ratio 0.87); at Δ<0.01 no effect (8/19, ratio 1.00) - decide by LN/depth instead. Activation-only matched pairs 19/28. q_b68ab2: plain SiLU RMSprop 1e-4×2048 (Δ0.2) beat residual LeakyReLU nets at larger Δ.

regime.note: delta = core-rule displacement (Adam/RMSprop lr*T, Adagrad 2lr*sqrt(T), SGD calibrated)

claims.text: UNIVARIATE regression, same MLP, Adam/AdamW vs RMSprop: Adam-family wins at almost any lr pairing - lab 78/88 same-arch within-set pairs (median MSE ratio ~0.06): equal lr 21/24; Adam at 3-33× LOWER lr 21/23; Adam at 3-10×+ higher lr 36/41. Adam lr≤RMSprop lr subset: non-oscillatory targets 15/15 (ratio 0.02), sin/cos(2πx) targets 27/32 (0.18). Corpus 4/5 (only loss: Adam 3e-5 vs RMSprop 3e-3, 100× gap). Do not credit RMSprop's early-step amplification (q_7f8fb0: AdamW 3e-5 beat RMSprop 3e-5 and 1e-4). Wide-net lr·T≥1 overshoot (K1055) still applies first. NOT multivariate (lab 10/18, ratio 0.97; corpus 5/9).

regime.note: lab mostly T=256, widths 64-192

claims.phase: Adam wins vs RMSprop by RMSprop/Adam lr ratio: 0.03-0.1: 18/21; 0.3: 18/20; 1: 21/24; 3-3.3: 12/14; 10: 7/7; 33: 2/2; corpus 100×: 0/1. Multivariate: 10/18 (no rule).

claims.text: Classification MLPs (tabular, XOR, spiral), NON-residual, depth≥2, all choices on the same SGD (plain or momentum): the net whose LAST hidden block has LayerNorm wins 31/31 lab within-set pairs (14 sets, median CE ratio 0.69) - even when it has FEWER LayerNorms in total (11/11, ratio 0.76). An unnormalized tail undoes earlier LN (q_1af0fa: a deep net with internal LN but 2 unnormalized final blocks lost to a shallower wider net; normalizing those blocks cut CE 0.69→0.47 in a controlled rerun). With adaptive optimizers the edge is weaker: Adam 70/102 (ratio 0.92), Adagrad 21/35 (~0.99). Regression: univariate 17/25, multivariate 20/35 - not reliable.
claims.mechanism: Under small SGD steps, update size scales with gradient magnitude; unnormalized ReLU/SiLU blocks after the last LN contract activations and backpropagated gradients, so the head and late layers barely move. Adaptive optimizers rescale per-parameter steps and largely cancel this attenuation, which predicts the much weaker edge under Adam/Adagrad (observed 0.92-0.99 ratios).
claims.phase: terminal-LN wins (nonresidual, depth≥2, classification): SGD 31/31 (0.69); Adam 70/102 (0.92); RMSprop 7/8; AdamW 6/11 (1.00); Adagrad 21/35 (0.99). Fewer-total-LN case: SGD 11/11, Adam 9/15.

claims.text: CLASSIFICATION MLPs (XOR/spiral/tabular), shared optimizer, Δ<0.1: RESIDUAL net vs NON-residual depth≥4 net with MORE LayerNorms — look at the plain net's LAST hidden block. Last block un-normalized → the residual net wins (lab SGD 16/16, CE ratio 0.72; adaptive 5/9; corpus 5/5): LNs followed by an unnormalized tail don't count. Last block LN'd → family-dependent: XOR+SGD plain wins 9/10; spiral+Adam-family plain wins 22/23 (residual CE ×1.3-1.4); spiral+SGD residual wins (lab 3/3, controlled 2/2, ratio 0.3-0.8); tabular ~coin flip (lab 12/27, corpus 6/6 plain). Moving LN to the last block (same count) lowered plain CE in 6/6 controlled cells.
claims.mechanism: An unnormalized final block after LN'd blocks re-shrinks/attenuates features right before the head, so the plain net's earlier LNs buy little; a residual path carries signal past it. Predicts: the effect vanishes once the plain tail is LN'd (observed), and weakens at larger Δ where every net trains (observed at Δ≥0.1).

regime.note: residual net has fewer LN than the deep plain net; same optimizer config for both; Δ>=0.1 mixed (spiral residual 6/13)

claims.phase: plain last-noLN: residual wins 26/30 (lab+corpus). plain last-LN: XOR-SGD plain 9/10; spiral-adaptive plain 22/23; spiral-SGD residual 3/3 (+2/2 controlled); tabular plain 12/27 lab, 6/6 corpus. Δ≥0.1 (adaptive): residual ~50% (spiral 6/13) — rule off.

claims.text: UNIVARIATE regression, RMSprop vs RMSprop (same MLP, different lr): the LOWER RMSprop lr usually wins, even at small Δ — lab larger-lr wins 9/42 (10 experiment groups; T=256 width≥128: 3/24, median MSE ratio 3.6; lr 1e-4 vs 3e-5: 3/11), corpus 2/3. At T=1024 on narrow nets it is a coin flip (4/9). RMSprop as the larger-Δ choice against Adam/AdamW of the same net also loses (lab 0/21 at RMSprop lr≥3e-4). Do not apply max-Δ to RMSprop on univariate MSE; multivariate is a coin flip (11/25).
claims.mechanism: PyTorch RMSprop has no bias correction and a zero-init square average (alpha 0.99), so early steps are ~lr/sqrt(1-0.99^t) ≈ up to 10× lr, kicking a 1-D smooth fit off its low-MSE basin; the transient matters most at short T, predicting the effect fades at T=1024 (observed: 4/9).

regime.note: mostly controlled experiment groups (10); T=1024 narrow nets near coin flip

claims.phase: larger RMSprop lr wins: T=256 w≥128 3/24; T=256 w≤96 2/9; T=1024 w≤96 4/9; multivariate 11/25 (no effect).

claims.text: XOR with ≥8 input features, once trained (shared optimizer, Δ≥0.05): depth helps only WITH residuals. A deeper NON-residual MLP loses to a shallower one even at a 1-2 block gap (lab deeper wins 1/31, 13 sets, CE ×1.23); a deeper RESIDUAL MLP beats a shallower one at a 1-2 block gap (8/13, 7 sets, CE ×0.82) but loses at gap ≥3 (lab 0/4, corpus 2-vs-5 block 2/3 shallow, K1018). q_164857 (AdamW 1e-4×2048): 3-block residual SiLU nets beat 1-block w192 nets, and the 3-block non-residual GELU net was last. At Δ<0.05 depth is a coin flip (plain 10/25, residual 14/19 deeper wins).

regime.note: gap>=3 residual evidence is 1 lab set + 3 corpus pairs

claims.phase: Δ≥0.05: deeper plain 1/31; deeper residual gap1-2 8/13, gap≥3 0/4 (+corpus shallow 2/3). Δ<0.05: deeper plain 10/25, deeper residual 14/19.

claims.text: TWO-SPIRAL classification, DEEP vs SHALLOW (same optimizer): a deeper (≥3 block) RESIDUAL MLP with MORE LayerNorms than a shallow (≤2 block) net wins almost always — lab 51/55 (adaptive Δ≥0.05 34/35, CE ratio 0.38; adaptive Δ<0.05 11/14; SGD 6/6, ratio 0.36), corpus 8/8 (ratio 0.76) — even if the shallow net is much wider. Deeper NON-residual nets are unreliable: lab 30/32 with more LN but corpus 0/7 (q_5fe255, q_774f6c had unnormalized last blocks) — credit them only if their last block is LN'd (K1061). Deeper residual with ≤ the shallow net's LN: lab 33/43, corpus 0/2 — tendency only. q_d7ea11: 3-LN residual deep net beat the shallow wide pick.

regime.note: pairs depth<=2 vs depth>=3 under identical optimizer; turns 1-2.5

claims.phase: deep residual, more LN: 59/63 (lab+corpus). deep residual, ≤LN: lab 33/43, corpus 0/2. deep plain: lab 75% / corpus 0/7 → use last-LN (K1061).

claims.text: BIGRAM LM post-LN TRANSFORMER d_model × Δ (same optimizer/lr/T, different d_model): wider wins only while under-trained; the flip is at Δ≈0.1. Δ 0.02-0.1: LARGER d_model wins (lab 21/23, corpus 13/13, CE ratio ~0.98). Δ 0.1-0.5 (e.g. Adam-family 3e-4 at T=512-1024): SMALLER d_model wins (lab 26/27 — d64 beat d128 20/21, d32 beat d128 2/2 with ratio 1.14; corpus 7/11, d64 vs d128 3/3). Δ≥0.5: smaller wins (lab 10/12, corpus 5/6). Δ<0.02: coin flip, SGD favors wider. Fills K1017's gap. q_02539d: d128 AdamW 3e-4×512 (Δ0.15) lost to d64 RMSprop 3e-3×512.

regime.note: post-LN, d_model 32/64/128

claims.phase: Larger d_model wins: Δ<0.02 lab 9/16 Adam-family, SGD 6/6; Δ 0.02-0.1 lab 21/23 + corpus 13/13; smaller wins Δ 0.1-0.5 lab 26/27 + corpus 7/11; Δ≥0.5 lab 10/12 + corpus 5/6.

claims.text: BIGRAM LM post-LN TRANSFORMER head count (same d_model/layers/optimizer/T): fewer heads (2 vs 4) wins 12/15 lab pairs. At Δ<0.5 it is only a tie-break (CE ratio ≈1.00); at Δ≥0.5 it matters (lab 4/4, ratio 1.01-1.07; controlled q_d6dddb d128 AdamW 3e-3×256: 2 heads −0.18 nats vs 4 heads, d_ff 128→256 only +0.07) and head count outranks a 2× d_ff difference (fewer heads + larger d_ff beat more heads + smaller d_ff 4/4). q_d6dddb gold: 2-head d_ff256 beat 4-head d_ff128. Order: d_model/layers (K1017) first, then heads, then d_ff.

regime.note: heads 2 vs 4; thin evidence (~15 lab pairs, 1 controlled)

claims.phase: Fewer heads wins: equal d_ff Δ<0.02 1/2, 0.02-0.5 4/4 (ratio 1.000), ≥0.5 2/2 (1.04); fewer heads with larger d_ff 4/4; fewer heads with smaller d_ff 1/3.

claims.text: CLASSIFICATION MLPs (spiral/XOR/tabular), RMSprop vs Adam/AdamW at the SAME lr, same net, T≤1024: RMSprop usually WINS — lab 17/20 matched pairs (median Adam/RMS CE ratio 1.12; XOR 1.31, tabular 1.20, spiral 1.12), controlled 7/8; epoch q_4c1af8, q_e4c256 (XOR 3e-4, 3e-5), q_ebfdb8 (tabular 1e-4). Treat RMSprop ≈ Adam at ~1.5× lr (Adam at 3.3× lr wins 5/9). Edge shrinks with T (tabular ratio 1.19 at T=256 → 1.04 at 1024; T=2048 Adam 1/1) and vanishes once CE≈0. At lr≤3e-4 also on multivariate regression (4/4) and bigram LM (4/4). At lr≥1e-3 Adam wins: bigram transformer 5/5 (ratio 1.02-1.08; q_a97a96 RMSprop 3e-3 last), multivariate 6/6; univariate regression always Adam (K1057).
claims.mechanism: PyTorch RMSprop (alpha=0.99) zero-inits its square-average without bias correction, so step t is inflated by 1/sqrt(1-0.99^t): cumulative multiplier ≈1.47 at T=256, 1.24 at 512, 1.12 at 1024, 1.06 at 2048. Under-trained CE rewards extra displacement, so the edge must shrink with T (confirmed) and flip where low loss rewards smooth steps (converged spiral, MSE regression). Adam at 1.5× lr closes the spiral gap at T=256 but not ~8% on tabular: no-momentum noise is a second factor.

regime.note: regression/LM only at lr<=3e-4; univariate regression excluded

claims.phase: Classification T=256: RMS 14/16 (ratio 1.12-1.31); T=512 2/2; T=1024 lab 1/1, controlled 3/4 (1.01-1.04); T=2048 0/1; converged spiral CE<0.003 Adam 2/2. Multivariate: lr≤3e-4 RMS 4/4, lr≥1e-3 Adam 6/6. Bigram: lr≤3e-4 RMS 4/4; lr≥1e-3 transformer Adam 5/5; GRU high-lr unmeasured. Univariate: Adam ~20/25.

claims.text: BIGRAM LM learning-rate sweet spot (same model; choices differ in optimizer/lr/T; Δ per K1001): past a model-specific optimum MORE Δ LOSES - the solver's most common LM miss. d32/d64 transformers and GRUs: optimum Δ≈0.1-0.3 (Adam-family 3e-4 at T=512-1024, 1e-3 at T=256; Adagrad 3e-3); ≥2× more Δ than a rival already at 0.1-0.3 loses (lab transformer 1/44, GRU 1/6, CE +2-20%); Δ≥1 loses to any rival with Δ≥0.03 (lab 0/17; q_c3a179). d_model=128 post-LN transformer: optimum ≈0.03-0.1; larger loses 0/11 once rival Δ≥0.03 (q_88802d AdamW 3e-3×256 last). Below the optimum max-Δ holds (13/13; GRU 14/15). Corpus: pick 'Δ nearest 0.2 (0.1 for d128)' 52/65 vs max-Δ 43/65.
claims.mechanism: Labels are sampled from P(y|x), so minibatch gradients carry irreducible noise; with a constant lr, once the V×V table is fit further displacement only adds noise-driven parameter jitter and memorisation of the 800 training windows (positions/contexts), raising test CE. More parameters per token (d_model 128) reach that fit point at smaller Δ, so the optimum shifts down with width - predicting d128 < d64 ≈ d32 optimum, as observed.

regime.note: same model within set; V 24-48, alpha 0.8-1.4, 800 windows, bs16; Δ<0.03 rivals: max-Δ applies

claims.text: Univariate MSE, SAME depth≥2 width≥64 MLP: Δ≥1 is an overshoot RISK relative to a well-progressed Δ≈0.1-0.5 rival, not automatic last place. Older corpus5/5; high-Δ lab wins w64 0/12 (MSE×8.8), w128 5/18 (×5.5), w256 1/13 (×4.4); controlled11/12 favor moderate Δ. Yet q_af3ba4's zero-LN width128 Adam Δ6.14 beat slower recipes (Δ0.027-0.205), losing only to AdamW Δ0.614; zero-LN architecture is not a validated exception. Against Δ<0.05 no universal cutoff is established (q_f609cc high-rate Adam won). Width≤32 (larger9/16), depth1 (8/8 lab,10/10 corpus), and multivariate (10/10 lab,4/5 corpus) lie outside the strong ceiling regime.
claims.mechanism: Adam-family steps are ≈lr per parameter regardless of gradient size, so the per-step change of the network function grows with fan-in and the number of stacked hidden matrices. A 1-D target on 256 points is fit by a wide multi-layer net within Δ≈0.1; further un-annealed lr-sized steps leave a minibatch-jitter MSE floor growing with lr·width. Predicts: narrow (≤32) or 1-layer nets stay progress-limited (max-Δ wins) and harder multivariate targets push the optimum up - both observed.

regime.note: width≤32 or depth 1: max-Δ holds; multivariate excluded

claims.phase: Same net, Δ_hi≥1 vs Δ_lo 0.1-0.5: larger wins w64 0/12, w128 5/18, w256 1/13 (controlled 1/12, corpus 0/5); w≤32 9/16; depth-1 8/8 (corpus 10/10). Δ_lo<0.05: low side wins only if Δ_hi≥5 (lab 3/7). Multivariate: larger wins 10/10 lab, 4/5 corpus.

claims.text: Tabular CE, 1024 rows: use epoch-dependent Δ optima for SAME-network optimizer/rate comparisons, NOT to reverse architecture differences automatically. E=examples_seen/1024. smooth_additive: E4 optimum≈0.25 (Δ0.77 lost to0.26, controlled3/3); E16≈0.08 (controlled2/2; q_c1581a); E32≈0.05-0.15 (Δ≥0.5 loses24/28 lab; ≥3× more wins1/15 when small Δ≥0.03). At E4 below Δ0.03, more wins56/56. sparse_interaction: optimum≈0.25 at E4-16,≈0.15 at E32; once smaller Δ≥0.1, larger wins5/33 (CE×1.44). piecewise larger wins10/10 at E16. q_7a5eba: shallow AdamW Δ0.256 beat deeper RMSprop Δ0.0768 at E16; cross-architecture optimum-based reversal is unvalidated.
claims.mechanism: Once the boundary is learned, extra displacement inflates logit norm and fits distractor directions on only 1024 rows; test CE punishes confident errors. Bigger batches over more epochs give cleaner gradients, so each unit of Δ fits training rows faster and the overfit point comes at smaller Δ. Sparse interactions need more movement to find the feature pair (higher optimum); axis-aligned piecewise boundaries keep gaining from sharper logits.

regime.note: 1024 train rows, 2-16 features; E=4 is bs16, E=16-32 bs64 (batch confounds epochs); controlled only on width-256 1-layer ReLU+LN net

claims.phase: smooth optimum Δ: E4 ≈0.25, E16 ≈0.08, E32 0.05-0.15. Larger(≥3×) wins: E4 small<0.03 56/56; E16 small≥0.1 smooth 2/2, piecewise 10/10, sparse 0/4; E32 smooth small 0.03-0.1 1/10, ≥0.1 0/5; Δ≥0.5 vs 0.01-0.15 at E32 smooth: low wins 24/28.

claims.text: REGRESSION DEPTH (univariate/multivariate MSE MLPs; picking the shallow-wide net is the most common univariate miss): a depth≥4 net with ≥1 LayerNorm (and ≥ the rival's LN count) beats a depth≤2 net - even a wider and/or residual one - whenever its core-rule Δ is ≥1/3 of the shallow net's: univariate corpus 31/38, lab 380/461 (MSE ratio ~0.15-0.2); multivariate corpus 18/22, lab 323/435 (~0.7). If deep Δ <1/3 of shallow Δ the shallow net wins (uni corpus 8/9, lab 228/295; multi 6/6, 159/215). Deeper residual beats shallower non-residual 32-2; deep-narrow beats shallow-wide 70-32. Deep NON-residual 0-LN stacks attenuate signal and usually lose.
claims.mechanism: Curved/oscillatory MSE targets need composed nonlinearities; each LN'd block restores unit-scale activations, so a deep stack keeps gradient and feature scale while composition builds curvature a 1-2 layer net reaches slowly. It is an optimisation-speed effect, so it needs comparable displacement: when deep Δ <1/3 of shallow Δ raw movement dominates (observed flip). Without LN or residuals deep plain stacks attenuate signal (observed losses).

regime.note: Δ ratio uses K1001/K1019 calibration; deep = depth≥4 with ≥1 LN

claims.phase: deep(≥4,≥1 LN) vs shallow(≤2): Δ_deep/Δ_shallow ≥1/3 → deep wins uni 380/461, multi 323/435; <1/3 → shallow wins uni 228/295, multi 159/215.

claims.text: Bigram LM at shared optimizer/lr/T: Δ0.02-0.05 has NO validated GRU/transformer rule. At Adam Δ0.0256, alpha0.8, q_8417bc favored a 2-layer GRU; alpha1.4 q_0c37d0 favored transformers. Do not extrapolate the near-frozen cutoff sharply. Δ<0.02: GRU wins on weak laws alpha≤1 (corpus8/8, controlled5/6). Δ0.05-0.1: equal/larger-width transformers won14/14 matched lab comparisons, but all from ONE set; q_9344eb also favored transformers at Δ0.0614. GRU64 vs transformer32 wins9/9 are width-confounded. At Δ0.1-0.5 older GRU wins8/9, and Δ≥0.5 3/3; these small samples are not width-independent laws. K1071 handles model-specific overshoot.
claims.mechanism: Both nets must learn a current-token lookup. When nearly frozen, the GRU's gates pass the input embedding straight to the output, so tiny updates already cut CE, while the transformer must first beat random positional embeddings and attention mixing. Once Δ≥0.02 the transformer's residual stream carries token identity and its FF fits the table faster than a 2-layer non-residual GRU; by Δ≥0.1 post-LN transformers overshoot (K1071), returning the edge to the GRU.

regime.note: Shared optimizer/lr/T; alpha/data/width/budget matter. Delta .02-.05 unresolved; .05-.1 matched lab support from one set only.

claims.phase: near-frozen versus partial-training calibration; boundary .02-.05 unresolved

claims.text: Multivariate symbolic MSE, BOTH calibrated Δ<0.1 and Δ ratio 0.5-2: lean toward a non-residual MLP with exactly one extra LayerNorm over a residual rival; a skip is not one full LN point. Within-set lab: higher-LN plain wins 23/31 pairs (25 sets), median MSE ratio 0.906; equal optimizer/lr subset 4/6, ratio 0.913. Matched optimizer/lr training history: 41/53 pairs in 32 questions, including q_1f04dc (Adagrad 13/18). Do NOT extend above Δ=0.1 (lab 5/13, ratio 1.054) or to univariate (low-Δ 17/34, ratio 0.989). Width, depth, activation and optimizer knobs remain confounded; this is a preference, not a causal LN effect.
